lead: An open control volume has streams crossing its boundary. Each stream carries entropy at rate m s. Heat crossing the boundary also carries entropy at rate Q/T. Inside, friction, mixing and finite gradients create extra entropy. The entropy balance adds these terms and says the entropy stored in the control volume changes by what flows in minus what flows out plus what is generated. At steady state the stored entropy does not change, so generation equals outlet entropy flow minus inlet entropy flow minus heat entropy flow. Engineers use it to test turbines, compressors, nozzles and heat exchangers for irreversibility.
prereq: You need: 3.4 Entropy and the steady-flow mass and energy balances from Unit 1.

blocks.text: Take a control volume (CV), a fixed region in space. Let m_i be mass flow at inlet i in kg/s and s_i its specific entropy in kJ/(kg·K). Let m_e and s_e be the same at outlet e. Let Q_j be heat rate into the CV across boundary j in kW, and T_j the absolute temperature of that boundary in K. Let S_CV be total entropy inside the CV in kJ/K, and S_gen the entropy generation rate in kW/K. The balance is:
dS_CV/dt = Σ m_i s_i − Σ m_e s_e + Σ Q_j/T_j + S_gen
blocks.where: S_CV is total entropy inside the CV in kJ/K; t is time in s; m_i is inlet mass flow in kg/s; s_i is inlet specific entropy in kJ/(kg·K); m_e and s_e are outlet mass flow and specific entropy; Q_j is heat rate into the CV in kW; T_j is the uniform absolute temperature of boundary j in K; if the boundary temperature varies, replace Q_j/T_j by the integral ∫ δQ/T over that boundary; S_gen is entropy generation rate in kW/K.

blocks.text: The first term is accumulation. The next two are entropy carried by flow. The heat term is entropy carried by heat; use T_j in kelvin. S_gen comes from irreversibility inside: friction, mixing, chemical reaction, heat transfer across a finite temperature difference. The second law gives S_gen ≥ 0, with equality only for a reversible process. S_gen is not a state property; it is fixed by the process. At steady state dS_CV/dt = 0, so S_gen = Σ m_e s_e − Σ m_i s_i − Σ Q_j/T_j. A negative computed S_gen means the data or sign convention is wrong.
For one inlet and one outlet, steady, adiabatic (Q_j = 0), the balance reduces to:

blocks.where: m is mass flow in kg/s; s_in and s_out are inlet and outlet specific entropies in kJ/(kg·K); S_gen is entropy generation rate in kW/K.

blocks.text: Work and kinetic energy do not appear: entropy crosses only with mass and heat. A real adiabatic turbine has s_out > s_in because friction and losses generate entropy; the ideal isentropic turbine sets s_out = s_in and S_gen = 0. A compressor needs work; if adiabatic, the same formula applies and real s_out > s_in. If the compressor is cooled, heat leaves, so Q_j is negative; use the full balance. A nozzle has no work and is often adiabatic: S_gen = m(s_out − s_in), and an ideal nozzle is isentropic.

For a two-stream heat exchanger with no external heat, enclose both streams in the CV. Then S_gen = m_h(s_h,out − s_h,in) + m_c(s_c,out − s_c,in). Internal heat from hot to cold stays inside the CV and does not appear as Q_j. If the exchanger also loses heat to the room, the leak raises the generation: S_gen = m_h(s_h,out − s_h,in) + m_c(s_c,out − s_c,in) − Q_room/T_room, with Q_room negative when heat leaves, so the last term is positive. Some syllabi call the steady balance the second law for a control volume.

items: Draw the CV and mark every inlet, outlet and heat crossing.
Write m and s for each stream, using kJ/(kg·K).
Write each Q_j as positive into the CV and T_j in K.
Put terms in the balance and solve for S_gen. Check units and sign.

blocks.text: Check units: kg/s × kJ/(kg·K) = kW/K; kW divided by K = kW/K. Check sign: S_gen cannot be negative. For a reversible adiabatic device, S_gen = 0. For a real adiabatic device, outlet specific entropy is greater than inlet. The same S_gen becomes lost work when multiplied by T₀; see 3.7 Irreversibility, lost work and ideal work.

figure.caption: Entropy enters with the inlet stream and with heat, leaves with the outlet stream, and is generated inside; at steady state the stored entropy does not change.

spec.title: Entropy balance on a control volume
spec.aria: Entropy enters a steady control volume with the inlet stream and heat transfer, leaves with the outlet stream, and is generated inside by irreversibility.

examples.question: Steam enters an adiabatic turbine. Take s_in = 7.0 kJ/(kg·K) and s_out = 7.4 kJ/(kg·K) as the given data (rounded for arithmetic). The mass flow is 2 kg/s. The turbine is steady and adiabatic. Find the entropy generation rate. State whether the turbine is reversible.
steps: Choose a CV around the turbine. Steady flow: dS_CV/dt = 0. One inlet, one outlet, adiabatic: Q_j = 0.
Write the balance: 0 = m s_in − m s_out + S_gen.
Convert units: 1 kJ/s = 1 kW, so S_gen = 0.8 kW/K.
examples.answer: S_gen = 0.8 kW/K. The positive value shows the turbine is irreversible, not isentropic.
examples.check:
m = 2.0
s_in = 7.0
s_out = 7.4
S_gen = m * (s_out - s_in)
print(S_gen)

traps: Forgetting S_gen and treating an adiabatic real turbine as isentropic. A real adiabatic turbine has s_out > s_in.
Reversing the order: for an adiabatic device, S_gen = m(s_out − s_in), not m(s_in − s_out). A negative answer is impossible.
Using the fluid temperature instead of the boundary temperature in Q_j/T_j. The temperature is the absolute temperature where heat crosses the CV boundary, in K.
Mixing up mass flow and total mass. m s has units kg/s × kJ/(kg·K) = kW/K; using kg instead of kg/s gives the wrong unit.
Setting S_gen = 0 for a two-stream heat exchanger because there is no external heat. Internal heat exchange can still generate entropy; add the entropy changes of both streams.

quiz.q: Define entropy generation rate S_gen and state its sign rule.
quiz.a: S_gen is the rate of entropy created inside a control volume by irreversibility, in kW/K. The second law requires S_gen ≥ 0, with equality only for a reversible process.

quiz.q: Why must s_out be greater than s_in for a real adiabatic turbine with one inlet and one outlet?
quiz.a: For steady adiabatic flow, S_gen = m(s_out − s_in). Since m > 0 and S_gen ≥ 0, s_out ≥ s_in. Friction and losses make the real turbine irreversible, so s_out > s_in.

quiz.q: Steam flows at 1.5 kg/s through an adiabatic nozzle. Inlet specific entropy is 6.8 kJ/(kg·K); outlet specific entropy is 7.1 kJ/(kg·K). Find S_gen.

An adiabatic two-stream heat exchanger has hot stream 1 kg/s with s_h,in = 2.0 and s_h,out = 1.6 kJ/(kg·K), and cold stream 1 kg/s with s_c,in = 0.8 and s_c,out = 1.3 kJ/(kg·K). Find S_gen and say whether the data are possible.
quiz.a: S_gen = 1(1.6 − 2.0) + 1(1.3 − 0.8) = −0.4 + 0.5 = 0.1 kW/K. It is positive, so the data are possible.

quiz.q: A compressor has m = 0.5 kg/s, s_in = 1.8 and s_out = 2.0 kJ/(kg·K). It loses 10 kW of heat at a boundary at 300 K. Find S_gen.
A claim says an adiabatic nozzle has s_out < s_in. Is this possible? Explain with the entropy balance.
quiz.a: No. For steady adiabatic one-inlet one-outlet flow, S_gen = m(s_out − s_in). If s_out < s_in, then S_gen < 0, which violates the second law. Therefore s_out ≥ s_in.

quiz.q: Write the steady-state entropy balance for a control volume with several inlets, outlets and heat crossings.
quiz.a: 0 = Σ m_i s_i − Σ m_e s_e + Σ Q_j/T_j + S_gen, or S_gen = Σ m_e s_e − Σ m_i s_i − Σ Q_j/T_j, with Q_j positive into the CV and T_j in K.

beyond: Not for the exam. In plant audits, entropy generation is computed stream by stream to rank irreversibility in a steam network; multiplying by dead-state temperature gives lost work. Exergy-based variants of heat-exchanger network pinch analysis also track entropy generation stream by stream to reduce utility use. Research uses local entropy generation in CFD to optimise ducts and compact exchangers. Search for 'entropy generation minimisation', 'lost work', and 'control volume second law'.
